applies_why: The judge text does not weigh a collision of chain against chain by footing; it disposes of C4 because the targeted curse limb was dropped, leaving no live link.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase "When the witnesses pressed against a link ... the collision weighs chain against chain by footing": I weighed whether it governs only a live-link collision (so a dropped limb means no K-C issue) or still requires chain-vs-chain weighing after a dropped limb.
why: The judge does not use a verse-by-verse stating-verse test; it says the pressed limb was dropped, so no live collision remains for K-C's chain-vs-chain weighing.
